name: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP)
eligibilitySummary: Income, resources, household circumstances, and other program rules are considered. The administering agency determines eligibility.
matchingNote: District poverty and income are outreach signals, not individual eligibility determinations.

name: Med-QUEST (Hawaiʻi Medicaid)
administeringAgency: Hawaiʻi Department of Human Services, Med-QUEST Division
whoItServes: Qualifying Hawaiʻi residents seeking medical coverage
eligibilitySummary: Eligibility depends on household and applicant circumstances, including income and categorical requirements; apply through Med-QUEST for a determination.
matchingNote: Economic need alone does not establish Medicaid eligibility or lack of insurance.

name: Women, Infants, and Children (WIC)
whoItServes: Qualifying pregnant, postpartum, or breastfeeding people, infants, and children under age five
eligibilitySummary: Income, participant category, and nutritional or medical risk requirements apply. A WIC clinic determines eligibility.
matchingNote: Matching is provisional until child age and relevant population indicators are added.

name: Hawaiʻi Home Energy Assistance Program (H-HEAP)
administeringAgency: Hawaiʻi Department of Human Services / participating Community Action Agencies
whoItServes: Qualifying households needing electric or gas bill assistance
eligibilitySummary: Income and other requirements apply; crisis intervention and energy credit have different application windows and processes.
matchingNote: High rent or poverty does not establish utility assistance eligibility.

name: Hawaiʻi Earned Income Tax Credit
whoItServes: Qualifying workers and families claiming the Hawaiʻi income tax credit
eligibilitySummary: Rules depend on earned income, tax filing circumstances, and related federal credit qualifications; refer to current state tax instructions.
matchingNote: District-level income and unemployment do not identify tax-credit eligibility or filing status.

name: Federal Earned Income Tax Credit
whoItServes: Qualifying workers and families with earned income
eligibilitySummary: Eligibility depends on earnings, filing status, investment income, identification, and other tax rules.
matchingNote: Income statistics alone cannot establish tax eligibility or unclaimed credits.

name: Kūpuna Care
administeringAgency: Hawaiʻi aging services network / county Area Agencies on Aging
whoItServes: Older adults with qualifying functional support needs who may benefit from home- and community-based services
eligibilitySummary: Generally serves people aged 60 or older meeting functional and other program requirements; service capacity and county procedures may vary.
matchingNote: County service page is specific to Honolulu; use the relevant county agency for other districts. Requires new age/disability data before automated matching.

name: Supplemental Security Income (SSI)
whoItServes: People who are age 65 or older, blind, or have a qualifying disability and have limited income and resources
eligibilitySummary: Age or disability criteria, income and resource limits, residency, and other federal requirements apply.
matchingNote: Census estimates cannot establish individual SSI eligibility. Requires new age/disability data before automated matching.

name: Medicare Savings Programs
administeringAgency: Hawaiʻi Medicaid program / Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services
whoItServes: Qualifying Medicare participants needing help with premiums and certain other costs
eligibilitySummary: Requirements differ among QMB, SLMB, QI, and QDWI; income, resources and Medicare enrollment are considered. Hawaiʻi limits may differ from federal figures.
matchingNote: Age, poverty, and disability indicators are outreach signals, not proof of Medicare enrollment or program eligibility.
